author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can narrow the veterinarian list to one specialty by address
summary: Both veterinarian list surfaces, the paged directory page and the machine-readable list, accept an optional specialty in the address and return only veterinarians holding it. Whole-name, case-insensitive match; an unmatched specialty yields an empty list; a blank one is ignored.
acceptance_criteria: given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when /vets.html is requested with ?specialty=<name>, then only those veterinarians are listed, and paging applies to the narrowed list
given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when /vets is requested with ?specialty=<name>, then the machine-readable list contains only those veterinarians
given a narrowed directory spanning more than one page, when a page is rendered, then every link between pages carries the specialty parameter
given a specialty differing from a held one only by letter case, when either surface is requested with it, then it matches
given only the start of a specialty name, when either surface is requested with it, then no veterinarian matches
given a specialty with leading or trailing spaces, when either surface is requested with it, then it matches the same specialty without them

given a specialty no veterinarian holds, including the word the directory shows for none, when either surface is requested with it, then HTTP 200 returns the normal page or document with an empty veterinarian list
given an empty or whitespace-only specialty, when either surface is requested with it, then the result equals the request without the parameter
given no specialty parameter, when either surface is requested, then it behaves exactly as today
a veterinarian holding several specialties appears in the list narrowed by any one of them
non_goals: any form, dropdown, link, or other page control for choosing a specialty on either surface (owner deferred to a possible follow-up request)
free-text or prefix search for a veterinarian (NG-9, narrowed)
naming more than one specialty in one request (open question in docs/prd.md)
stating the active specialty on the narrowed directory page (open question in docs/prd.md; narrowest reading: the page changes only in which veterinarians it lists)
any change to veterinarians or specialties themselves (NG-2)
notes: PRD edits this dispatch: minted REQ-VET-003 (the filter) and REQ-VET-004 (the machine-readable list reinstated as a supported surface, per the owner's intake decision; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and is mapped to REQ-VET-004 as successor in Superseded). REQ-VET-004's unfiltered behavior already exists and is covered by the existing machine-readable list test; this slice adds no REQ-VET-004 behavior. Removed REQ-VET-001 edge case 2 (the stale known-defect note on the machine-readable route); it was the last item, so no renumbering. Narrowed NG-9 per the owner's decision and recorded non-goal ADR docs/adr/2026-09-18-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md. For system-design-expert: docs/adr/README.md index needs a row for that ADR (outside my write scope); system-design.md still says there is no JSON API for primary workflows and maps the Vets wrapper to no requirement, so the wrapper now traces to REQ-VET-004. Test names group data-driven cases: case-insensitivity, prefix non-match, and surrounding spaces share one test across both surfaces.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the vet feature package unchanged (system-design.md § Package Structure): controller -> repository, no service layer, per the Feature-Package ADR. New ground: the filter is a derived query on VetRepository, offered paged (directory page) and unpaged (machine-readable list), matching the whole Specialty name ignoring case, and deliberately NOT cached (ADR 2026-09-18-specialty-filter-as-uncached-repository-query). VetController binds an optional `specialty` request parameter, strips it, and treats a blank value as absent. That is binding under the architecture-principles.md Web controller row, mirroring owner search's strip in OwnerController.processFindForm. It then delegates to the narrowed or the unfiltered lookup. Matching semantics live in the query, never in the controller. The machine-readable /vets route is now a supported surface (REQ-VET-004), so the Overview, Contracts, Known Defects, Security Context and Threat Model rows were updated. Basis: grep and file reads of VetController, VetRepository, Vet, Specialty, Vets, vetList.html, CacheConfiguration, VetControllerTests and ClinicServiceTests. The IDE oracle was not connected, so this is the weaker basis.
integration_points: Binding target (both routes): a request-scoped `@RequestParam(required = false) String specialty` scalar. No persisted type is bound, and no binder disallow list is needed because no object is bound.

Repository boundary, matching semantics (case-insensitive, whole-name/prefix non-match, several specialties, the word 'none'): use the REAL VetRepository on the seeded H2 database, either through MockMvc in a @SpringBootTest + @AutoConfigureMockMvc test or through the @DataJpaTest pattern in ClinicServiceTests. A stub cannot observe these semantics. The seed gives radiology to two vets, surgery to two, and dentistry to one; one vet holds both surgery and dentistry, and some vets hold none.

Repository boundary, controller-only behavior (blank/whitespace treated as absent, stripping before delegation, page links carrying the parameter, empty-result HTTP 200): the existing @MockitoBean VetRepository in the @WebMvcTest VetControllerTests may be extended as a framework stub. Reason: the class's slice context already replaces the repository, and no specialty in the seeded data spans more than one page (page size 5), so only a stubbed multi-page Page can exercise the link test. Prefer asserting on what was rendered over verify()-style interaction checks where the rendered output shows the behavior.
Framework transport: MockMvc (the sanctioned harness) for both /vets.html and /vets (JSON via Accept: application/json).

patterns.description: strip-then-query normalization of a search parameter at binding; blank means the broadest query
paged Spring Data derived query taking a Pageable; the narrowed lookup follows the same shape (e.g. a Distinct...BySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase form, name chosen by the implementer)
narrowed lookups carry no @Cacheable; only the unfiltered lookups use the vets cache

risks.risk: Narrowed lookups on both surfaces scale with the number of veterinarians (system-design.md § Scale and Load, row 'Either veterinarian list narrowed to one specialty': size unrecorded, treated as bounded)
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: one derived query per request, paged in the database for the directory page; no in-memory filtering or hand-written paging

risks.risk: Caching the narrowed lookups would make caller-supplied specialty strings keys in the size-unlimited `vets` cache (system-design.md § Threat Model, 'Cache growth through request-supplied keys'; security-principles.md Realization, 'Widening the exposed surface' / least privilege)
The specialty value reaches the database (security-principles.md Realization, 'Injection into data access')
risks.mitigation: Derived query parameter binding only; no concatenated JPQL/SQL

risks.risk: The specialty value is written into page-link hrefs (security-principles.md Realization, 'Cross-site scripting'; trust boundary 'External input arrives'). Thymeleaf `__${...}__` preprocessing of a request-derived value is an expression-injection vector, and string-concatenated hrefs leave the value un-URL-encoded.
risks.mitigation: Carry the parameter with Thymeleaf link-expression parameters (e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}), which URL-encode. Never preprocess the specialty value. Keep default escaping.

risks.risk: 'Without the parameter both endpoints behave as today' (REQ-VET-003 Done-when; PRD acceptance): the unfiltered page's links must not gain an empty or valueless specialty parameter
risks.mitigation: Expose the normalized specialty to the model only when present, and emit the link parameter only then. Check Thymeleaf's rendering of null-valued link parameters in the test for the unfiltered page.

risks.risk: Case-insensitive matching diverging per database vendor, as in the PostgreSQL owner-search defect (system-design.md § Known Defects, § Persistence)
risks.mitigation: Use the derived IgnoreCase form, which case-folds both sides in the query and does not depend on column collation (ADR 2026-09-18-specialty-filter-as-uncached-repository-query)

risks.risk: A vet appearing twice in a narrowed page if the join yields duplicate rows (PRD edge case 2, a vet holding several specialties)
risks.mitigation: Use a distinct derived query so the paged count and content count each vet once

notes: Design-doc follow-ups from the prd-entry notes are done. The ADR README index gained rows for the non-goal ADR and the new ADR. The Overview no longer denies every JSON surface. The Vets wrapper now traces to REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004. The stale Known Defects row for the unused machine-readable route was removed. Contracts: REQ-VET-003 joins the Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository and VetController rows; REQ-VET-004 joins the Vet, Vets, VetRepository, VetController and CacheConfiguration rows. Added § Scale and Load, which the design doc lacked, with three veterinarian-list rows. Security Context inputs and outputs and the Threat Model gained the specialty parameter and a cache-growth row. docs/adr/2026-09-18-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md is the product-requirements-expert's write, not this dispatch's; it is not claimed here. Brief gap for the security-principles.md owner: the Realization table has no row for template-engine expression preprocessing of request-derived values. The risk above covers this slice only. No design-doc-autofix records exist, so the audit was skipped. The page parameter's existing range behavior (page < 1, or page past the end) is unchanged and out of scope.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: SQL injection: the specialty value reaches the database only as a bound parameter of Spring Data derived queries (VetRepository.java: `Collection<Vet> findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String specialtyName)` and its Pageable overload); no string-built query text in the diff (read via `git diff -- src/main`).

XSS / template-expression injection: vetList.html never renders the specialty as text; it enters page links only through Thymeleaf link-expression parameters (`@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}`), which URL-encode the value. The diff also removes the prior `__${i}__` preprocessing from every pager link, so no request-derived value reaches preprocessing.

Cache-growth DoS: both specialty-narrowed repository methods are deliberately left without @Cacheable (VetRepository.java Javadoc: `Not cached: the name is caller-supplied`), so a caller cannot add keys to the unbounded `vets` cache; system-design.md Threat Model row 185 records this control.

Input handling at the boundary: `normalized()` strips the value and treats blank as absent on both routes; an unknown name yields an empty result rather than an error, so no exception message reaches the error page; no new request-bound @ModelAttribute/@RequestBody targets, so no mass-assignment surface.
No new endpoints: both handlers keep their existing GET routes and gain one read-only optional parameter; repository methods are @Transactional(readOnly = true).
No secrets added: grep of the changeset for password|secret|token|apikey|credential matched only the documentation line on datasource env credentials (system-design.md Security Context), no values.

Supply chain: build.gradle/pom.xml unchanged (`git diff --stat -- build.gradle pom.xml` empty). The runtime classpath resolves thymeleaf-spring6 3.1.5.RELEASE and tools.jackson jackson-databind 3.1.5. dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured, so no NVD match ran in this review.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The same `${specialty != null} ? @{/vets.html(page=X,specialty=${specialty})} : @{/vets.html(page=X)}` conditional is repeated verbatim (varying only the page value) across all four pagination links (grep -F -e 'specialty != null' -- src/main/resources/templates/vets/vetList.html confirms 4 hits, lines 30, 35, 40, 45, 50 — five link occurrences across four link elements). Checklist: 'A conditional repeated across sibling sites (code, template elements, links) is duplication: compute it once (th:with or a fragment) and reference it.' The ternary itself is necessary — Thymeleaf's @{} link syntax renders a null-valued parameter as an empty `specialty=` rather than omitting it (confirmed against Thymeleaf's documented behavior; the parameter must be built conditionally to satisfy the 'no specialty param on the unfiltered page' acceptance bullet) — but the four call sites should not each restate it.
findings.fix: Extract a th:fragment (e.g. th:fragment="pageLink(page)" in this template or a shared fragment file) that builds the href once from `specialty` and `page`, and call it from all four link elements with th:replace/th:insert, or bind the recurring condition to a single th:with-scoped variable read by all four hrefs.

recommendations: VetController.findPaginated and normalized take/build java.util.Optional<String> as a method parameter/return threaded through a private helper (VetController.java:50,65,84); Optional as a parameter type is a discouraged idiom (Effective Java item 55) even though no existing code in this module does otherwise — worth a plain String/boolean-narrowed pair if this seam grows further, but low-impact here since both methods are private and the flow reads clearly.
approved_aspects: VetController.normalized() and the two-argument findPaginated() keep matching and stripping logic out of the controller and read at one level of abstraction (src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/VetController.java:47-86)

VetRepository's two new derived-query methods carry accurate Javadoc explaining the deliberate absence of @Cacheable, consistent with docs/adr/2026-09-18-specialty-filter-as-uncached-repository-query.md (src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/VetRepository.java:58-77)
./gradlew checkFormat and ./gradlew compileJava compileTestJava both pass clean on the working tree

author: change-grader
summary: filter the vet directory and JSON list by specialty

blast_radius.note: Contained to the vet package (controller, repository, one template) plus PRD/design/ADR prose; no sensitive paths, one module, though both a public page and the reinstated /vets JSON endpoint gain a request parameter.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading the hunks, the filter does what the PRD says: blank or whitespace specialty normalizes to absent and falls back to the unchanged cached findAll paths, the new derived queries are distinct, whole-name, case-insensitive and deliberately uncached, and the round-2 pageLink fragment reproduces each original link's href, title and icon class with the specialty added only when present.

test_adequacy.note: The repository query is well pinned against real seeded data (case, partial name, the none word, distinct totalElements), but controller tests stub the repository, and the round-2 rewrite of all five pagination links into a th:replace fragment is asserted only through one page=2 href; first/previous links, titles and icon classes are unasserted, and the test-reviewer was not re-dispatched for that fix delta.
